answer: Because the juniper ledger attributes every share, the nectar audit publishes the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. Only 46% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not forfeit. A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, and therefore it burns the ripple fee twice and still divides one payout. That is 6 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
